questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: First and foremost, Singapore seemed as an exotic and interesting location, which is located in the middle of South East Asia with great oppourtunities to visit other interesting countries. Further, the university is ranked as Asia's best law school and one of the best law schools in the world, which was a big draw for me.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The university sent out a lot of information in the months leading up to the start of the semester and that information contained everything needed.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: No assistance was required as the email sent out from the university contained everything needed.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: You go through an application process where you rank your wishes for on-campus housing from a list of different housing options. Different colleges and houses etc. were available to pick from.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: My housing had a set meal plan providing breakfast and dinner 6 days a week. Further, there was a shared cooking facility (buttery) available.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: You are not guaranteed housing and if you are not lucky enough to secure on-campus housing then you must apply for private housing.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It is a multi-step process which begins before you arrive at NUS and is completed once you arrive by booking a timeslot in which you must physically registrate. This process is explained in detail in the emails received from the university and the completition of the process is easy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Hotlines etc.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I had to registrate for 4 classes and I was only successful in registering for two of my originally 4 requested courses. However, I was able to select my remaining two courses from a list of available courses, which was perfectly fine.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Follow the guidelines provided in the emails.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses corresponded with 3rd year BA electives or MA electives. The level was perfectly fine and I did not find the courses to be more difficult than the ones offered at UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I found the teaching style to be overall similar to UCPH but also very dependent on the specific professor.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Law of Money and Central Banking, Competition Law, Principles of Financial Law, Law and Practice of Investment Management.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would heavily recommend the abovementioned first three courses as I learned a lot and the courses were very well taught and extremely interesting. However, I would stay clear of the latter course as it was a big dissapointment.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Public transport is very cheap and Grab (same as Uber) is available.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything that you can think of.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Engage in the social activities offered and sign up for any student clubs that you may find interesting.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel all over South East Asia. Singapore has an amazing airport and you can easily and cheaply visit other nearby destinations during your weekends.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness and welcoming attitude.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1) Make an effort in the beginning of the semester to meet other exchange students and try and form relationships to other exchange students as well as local students. 2) Travel as much as you can during and after the semester. 3) Have a good time and enjoy yourself during your exchange - and focus more on the social aspects rather than the academic aspects.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The widening of my perspective and my encounter with so many wonderful cultures and people from all over the world.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
